Square POS **is the [best POS system for small and growing restaurants](http://tech.co/pos-system/best-pos-systems-for-small-businesses)**, due to its affordable pricing options, and robust set of tools for selling and scaling.

With its advanced hospitality features, such as tip-sharing and cost controls, **Toast is a better option for established, full-service restaurants**.

Clover POS, meanwhile, is the best option for **quick-service restaurants**, due to its durable, spill-resistant hardware, slick backend, and low transaction fees.

To inform this guide, our researchers tested **16 of the top POS systems** **across 40 user testing sessions**. You can find our thoughts below.

Key Takeaways

*   **Square POS is ideal for small businesses** seeking affordability and broad functionality, offering a free plan, cheap, durable card readers and a super-easy setup process, particularly for iPad users.
*   **Toast is best suited for established, full-service restaurants**, providing strong hospitality features like tip-sharing and cost controls. The only catch is that it’s an Android-exclusive system.
*   **Clover POS** is the best POS platform for quick-service restaurants, due to its easy-to-use interface, range of hardware, and low transaction fees.
*   **Consider transaction fees**, hardware compatibility (iOS versus Android), and the availability of advanced, industry-specific features when choosing a POS system for your business. Toast will not be suitable for retail businesses, for instance.
*   **While Square and Toast offer free entry-level plans**, comprehensive features like 24/7 support or advanced reporting often require upgrading to paid tiers.

Why Trust Us? Our Research Methodology

To bring you this and our other reviews, we’ve tested **16 POS systems over the course** **of** **40 user testing sessions**, which amounted to **720 hours** of testing in total.

We asked our test participants to carry out a range of preset tasks on each POS system and describe their user journey in detail.

We also developed a **detailed methodology** that focuses on **six core categories of investigation** — software features (30%), hardware (15%), pricing (10%), ease of use (20%), help and support (15%), and reputation (10%). These categories were broken down into a further **41 subcategories**.

**AI can’t test POS systems**, so we don’t think it should write reviews about them either. That’s why 100% of Tech.co’s reviews are researched, written, and edited by humans.

# Toast vs. Square: A Head-to-Head Comparison

In this article, I’m diving into two top point-of-sale (POS) systems for restaurants: Toast vs. Square. I’ll cover the pricing, features, hardware options, and customer service for each.

14 min readApril 1, 2025

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69b9330c8b70142e4e5f7d3d/69b9330c8b70142e4e5f88f9_toast-vs-square-thumbail%20\(1\).jpg)

Key takeaways

*   Advanced features and scalability make Toast perfect for high-volume operations, but it can be costly for smaller businesses.
*   Square is simple, affordable and easy to set up, ideal for quick-service restaurants and startups.
*   A good POS system with a strong online ordering plan can boost restaurant profits. It also cuts down on their need for third-party platforms.

‍

Many owners compare Toast vs. Square when choosing a POS system for their restaurant. From my work with restaurant owners on tech solutions, I’ve seen that this choice goes beyond just payment processing—it’s about improving operations and saving time. 

Both systems are popular, but they serve different types of businesses. Understanding their differences is key to choosing the right one for your restaurant, ensuring you get the best value and most efficient functionality tailored to your specific needs.

In this post, I'll guide you through comparing Toast and Square by exploring pricing, features, payment processing and customer support to help you choose the best system for your business.

## **Toast: Best for simplifying back-office operations**

Toast is a powerful POS system that simplifies back-office tasks, making it ideal for full-service restaurants and businesses with multiple locations. Its wide range of tools helps improve everything from menu creation to reporting and employee scheduling, while tracking food waste, inventory and sales in real time.

 ![A graphic displaying a list of Toast’s pros and cons](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666eec3edcc552b5eecc7fcd/67ec6584adeb470104fef742_toast-pros-and-cons-mobile.png)

Toast's commission-free [online ordering system](https://www.owner.com/blog/online-ordering-system-for-restaurants) and delivery help restaurants increase online sales without third-party platforms or extra fees.

The system offers features like multi-location management, centralized reporting, food waste tracking and customizable tools that can adapt as your restaurant expands. 

Toast also works well with other tools, like accounting software and loyalty programs. This makes it more versatile than Square.

**Key features:**

*   **Checkout and tableside ordering** for faster, more efficient service
*   **Customizable menus** that can handle complex offerings for dine-in, takeout and delivery
*   **Flexible website tools** designed to increase dine-in reservations and customer engagement
*   **Seamless integrations** with third-party apps, accounting software and loyalty programs
*   **Streamlined hardware** tailored for restaurant needs

Toast offers 24/7 support for all plans, though customer feedback is mixed, and it may not always meet expectations. Its hardware is more tailored to restaurants compared to Square, making it an ideal choice for complex, scalable restaurant operations. 

The system's strong integrations help optimize all aspects of the business, making it a highly customizable POS system for restaurants.

| --- | --- |
| Ease of use | 4.2 |
| Value for money | 3.9 |
| Available features | 4.1 |
| Customer service | 3.7 |

[**Rating Source**](https://www.owner.com/comparison/toast-vs-owner)

**Customers like:**

_“Toast is the best. It is constantly improving. Very user friendly. Very flexible to suit your way your business works. Excellent customer support. But comes with a price.”_

_“Toast provides a wonderful technology and great incentives to help other restaurants get the same advantages with their software. Great folks!”_

**Customers don’t like:**

_“The system works well; if your processes are setup how toast wants you to operate. The reporting tools are trash. Huge improvements needed in analytics and reporting.”_

_“Customer Service is amazing. They always try to help with any issue. Unfortunately, on boarding was very painful for us.”_

## **Square: Best for new restaurants**

[Square](https://squareup.com/us/en/point-of-sale) is an excellent option for new restaurants looking for an affordable and flexible POS system. It's great for beginners or anyone on a tight budget. You can check out my latest guide on [Square POS cost](https://www.owner.com/blog/square-pos-system-cost) for more of an idea.

It offers a free plan with basic features, which helps you manage cash flow before you commit. Square has no long-term contracts and flat processing rates are 2.6% plus 10 cents for each transaction. This makes it easy to predict your costs.

 ![A graphic displaying a list of Square’s pros and cons](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666eec3edcc552b5eecc7fcd/67ec663de07b50c4750a7810_square-pros-and-cons-mobile.png)

For small, single-location restaurants, Square provides everything needed to run daily operations efficiently. It’s a budget-friendly choice that also offers a mobile app for on-the-go management. Toast has launched branded [mobile apps](https://www.owner.com/blog/mobile-app-for-restaurants) for its Premium plan. 

However, Square’s app is open to all users, making it more accessible. Plus, its menu, inventory and tableside management tools help you simplify operations. 

**Key features:**

*   **Inventory and tableside management** to streamline operations and improve service
*   **Menu management tools** to easily update and customize offerings for dine-in, takeout and delivery
*   **Payment processing** with transparent flat-rate fees and no hidden costs
*   **Seamless integrations** with third-party apps, accounting software and loyalty programs
*   **Affordable mobile app** available for easy management on the go

Square offers strong integrations with a variety of third-party apps, allowing you to customize your system with different tools. However, Toast is an integrated solution, meaning it comes with a broader set of built-in features and doesn’t rely on third-party apps for its core functionality. 

This can simplify things for restaurants that prefer an all-in-one system without the need for additional integrations. Square offers 24/7 support, but its customer service may lack the depth of Toast’s restaurant-focused help. 

Square offers simple back-office features, making it easy to use. However, it lacks the food waste tracking that Toast provides. Square's low prices and easy-to-use tools make it a great choice for new, single-location restaurants.

# Toast vs Square for Restaurants: Which POS Wins in 2026?

2026-06-09 • Tom Lawton

![](/images/blog/toast-vs-square-for-restaurants/toast-vs-square-for-restaurants.webp)

**Toast vs Square** is the closest thing the restaurant POS market has to a coin-flip question, and the honest answer is that neither system wins outright. Toast is built for restaurants and nothing else: restaurant-grade hardware, full-service workflows like coursing and floor plans, and a kitchen display system as a core product. Square is the fastest POS to start with, publishes every price on its website, carries no long-term contract, and runs food, retail, and hybrid operations on one platform. The right pick depends on your operation, not on a reviewer's scorecard.

One thing to know up front: Chowly partners with both. We integrate natively with [Toast](https://chowly.com/pos/chowly-for-toast/) and natively with [Square](https://chowly.com/pos/chowly-for-square/), we do not sell either system, and our platform works the same on both. Most comparisons in this category are written by companies selling against one side or both. This one is not.

**Quick answer:** Choose Toast if you run a full-service restaurant with servers on the floor, multiple kitchen stations, and complex ticket flow — it is purpose-built for exactly that. Choose Square if you run counter service, a cafe, a food truck, or a food-plus-retail hybrid and want the lowest-friction start with published pricing and no long-term contract. Then put real demand behind whichever one you pick, because the POS runs the register — it does not fill it.

## Square vs Toast at a Glance

|     | Toast | Square for Restaurants |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Built for | Restaurants only | Restaurants, retail, beauty, services |
| Entry plan | Starter Kit — $0/mo | Free — $0/mo |
| Paid plans | Point of Sale $69/mo; New Restaurant Basics from $110/mo; Build Your Own (quote) | Plus $49/mo per location; Premium $149/mo per location; Pro (custom) |
| In-person processing | 2.49% + 15¢ standard; 2.99% + 15¢ on pay-as-you-go | 2.6% + 15¢ (Free); 2.5% + 15¢ (Plus); 2.4% + 15¢ (Premium) |
| Online ordering | Commission-free add-on, flat monthly fee by quote | Branded ordering page included on every plan, including Free |
| Hardware | Restaurant-grade; kit pricing by quote; $0-upfront option available | Published prices, $59 Reader to $899 Register |
| Contract | 2-year agreement on the pay-as-you-go option; other terms set at quote | No long-term contract — cancel or switch plans anytime |
| Works with Chowly | Yes — POS-native | Yes — POS-native |

Every number in this article comes from each company's official pricing pages as of June 2026. Rates and plans change, so confirm current figures on [Toast's pricing page](https://pos.toasttab.com/pricing) and [Square's restaurant pricing page](https://squareup.com/us/en/point-of-sale/restaurants/pricing) before you sign anything.

## What Toast Does Best

Toast sells to one industry: restaurants. That focus shows up everywhere in the product. The hardware is built for kitchen conditions — heat, grease, drops, fourteen-hour days. Handheld terminals let servers fire orders and take payment at the table. The kitchen display system is a core product, not a bolt-on app. And the full-service workflows other systems treat as edge cases — coursing, seat-level check splitting, floor plan management, menu dayparting — sit at the center of the platform.

The reporting depth matches. Because Toast only thinks about restaurants, its analytics are organized around restaurant questions: menu item performance, daypart trends, labor against sales, channel mix. For an operator running a full-service room with a bar program and a busy kitchen, that specificity compounds every week.

Entry pricing is more accessible than Toast's reputation suggests. Per Toast's published pricing as of June 2026, the Starter Kit plan is $0/month, the Point of Sale plan is $69/month, and New Restaurant Basics — a POS-plus-payroll bundle aimed at new operators — starts at $110/month. Standard in-person processing is 2.49% + 15¢. Toast also offers a pay-as-you-go option: hardware costs covered at $0 upfront in exchange for a higher 2.99% + 15¢ processing rate and a 2-year agreement, currently offered to new single-location customers. For an operator who would rather protect opening-week cash than minimize per-swipe cost, that is a legitimate trade — just go in knowing the terms.

The honest trade-offs: hardware kits, online ordering, kiosk, and most add-ons are priced by quote, so getting your true all-in monthly number requires a sales conversation. And because Toast is restaurant-only, a hybrid operation — a cafe that also sells beans, mugs, and merch, for example — is outside its lane.

## What Square Does Best

Square's defining trait is how little stands between you and your first transaction. You can sign up self-serve, plug a $59 Reader into your phone, and take payments the same day. The Free plan costs genuinely $0/month and includes a [branded online ordering](https://chowly.com/solutions/branded-online-ordering/) page — something most POS systems charge for — so a new operator can be live with direct online ordering before the signage is up.

Transparency is the other differentiator. Every plan, every processing rate, every hardware device, and every per-device app fee is published on Square's website. As of June 2026: the Free plan is $0/month, Plus is $49/month per location, Premium is $149/month per location, and Pro is custom-priced for operations processing over $250K per year. In-person processing is tiered by plan — 2.6% + 15¢ on Free, 2.5% + 15¢ on Plus, 2.4% + 15¢ on Premium. Hardware runs from the $59 Reader through the $149 Stand, $299 Terminal, and $399 Handheld up to the $899 Register. You can price your entire setup from your couch, and there is no long-term contract on any plan — Plus and Premium even carry a 30-day free trial.

That flexibility extends to what you sell. Because Square spans restaurants, retail, and services, it handles hybrid operations naturally — the bakery with a retail shelf, the brewery with a merch wall, the food truck that does festival pop-ups.

The honest trade-offs: restaurant-specific depth thins at the edges. The kitchen display system is a per-device subscription — $30/month per device on Plus, $20/month on Premium — rather than a core product, kiosk is likewise $50 or $30 per device monthly, and ingredient-level inventory requires the MarketMan integration at $99/month per location. Square is a strong restaurant POS inside a platform that serves many industries, which means the deepest full-service workflows are not its center of gravity.
